From: Maya Singh <maya@bluefjord.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing for Zephyr model (32k)

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Based on our usage traces I attached a CSV with token distribution and average session lengths. We're looking at migrating a real-time summarization feature to a dedicated pool; the model is a 32k FFN-based Zephyr variant (we'll be testing 2 precisions: fp16 and int8/q4).

Key asks from our side:
- Rough GPU count and memory per-pod estimate for 150 concurrent sessions (p50 latency target 120ms).
- Impact of maintaining a 32k KV cache per session vs offloading to shared cache.
- Any guidance on quantization tradeoffs we should expect for quality-sensitive prompts.

I've copied ops@bluefjord.ai for telemetry. Appreciate any initial sizing you can share — we need this for our procurement doc by next week.

Thanks,
Maya Singh\VP Engineering, BlueFjord
(attachment: bluefjord-observed-profiles.csv)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@bluefjord.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 12:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for Zephyr model (32k)

Hi Maya —

Really helpful data, thanks. Looping in Karthik and Marcus from our capacity and runtime teams to give a model-specific estimate. High-level observations from the CSV: a long-tail of sessions near 20–25k tokens, with ~12% exceeding 28k. That argues for keeping a full KV per session for strict p50 latency targets unless we accept higher p99s.

Preliminary answers (will follow with numbers after Karthik runs the sim):
- Baseline: Zephyr-32k fp16: ~40GB device memory footprint for model + KV headroom; int8/q4 can reduce model memory by ~30–45% depending on activation/embedding storage layout.
- KV cache: a full 32k KV per active session (no offload) adds ~8–12GB of host memory pressure per 100 active sessions depending on streaming chunk size; keeping KV on-GPU (pinned) gives lowest latency but increases reserved device memory and reduces effective pods per GPU.
- Offload/shared-KV: good compromise for cost — offloading KV to host/NVMe reduces device footprint but adds 40–120ms depending on pattern; caching hot prefixes reduces this in practice.

Marcus/Karthik — can you run a quick sim with the attached profiles and the three scenarios: (A) fp16 with per-session on-GPU KV, (B) int8/q4 with per-session on-GPU KV, (C) fp16 with KV offload + prefix caching. Please include GPU-per-pod and recommended pod-per-GPU packing and expected p50/p95 latency.

I'll schedule a 30m follow-up with BlueFjord next Tue to review.

— Vanessa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-kv-sim-3scenarios.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for Zephyr model (32k)

Vanessa / Marcus —

Ran two quick simulations (local kernel-config + KV model). Notes below (high-level numbers, will validate with longer sim later):

Scenario A — fp16, per-session on-GPU KV:
- Model resident memory: ~42GB (includes tokenizer buffers, KV pointers).
- KV per active session (32k, 128-bit kv entry representation compressed-ish): ~850MB/session (we use chunked chunking -> roughly 27 chunks).
- Effective pods per 48GB GPU: 0.5 (i.e., one pod requires >1 GPU), so you'd need ~2 GPUs per pod unless we move to larger GPU (80GB+).
- For 150 concurrent sessions: ~255GB aggregate device memory required => ~6x A100-80GB (rounded). Latency: p50 ~110ms, p95 ~240ms.

Scenario B — int8/q4 model variant, per-session on-GPU KV:
- Model resident memory: ~24–28GB depending on quant layout and KV packing.
- KV still ~850MB/session (KV size dominated by context, not model precision).
- Effective pods per 48GB GPU: 1 pod fits on 48–80GB depending on exact model bits; with int8 we estimate 1 pod/GPU for 48GB class for single pod configs.
- For 150 sessions: aggregate device memory ~128GB => ~3x 48GB GPUs. Latency: p50 ~130ms (slightly higher due to quant-dequant), p95 ~300ms.

Scenario C — fp16 with KV offload + prefix caching:
- Model resident memory: ~42GB.
- On-GPU KV reserved only for hot prefixes (top ~15% sessions) — average effective KV on GPU ~130MB/session.
- Offloaded KV adds host NVMe bandwidth needs; measured additional tail latency ~60–110ms depending on cache hit.
- For 150 sessions: ~2–3x 48GB GPUs (depends on how aggressive caching is). Latency: p50 ~140ms with good prefix caching, p95 ~260–360ms (depends on NVMe cold hits).

Operational comments:
- Quantization wins are model-dependent; memory reduction is meaningful but KV size remains the dominant term for long contexts.
- If BlueFjord can accept p50 140ms and p95 ~300ms, int8 variant with aggressive pruning of inactive KV yields the best cost outcome.
- Recommend a 2-week staging run on a 3-GPU cluster with 1.5x the expected concurrency to surface tail behavior and slot packing edge cases.

I'll export the sim logs and a per-GPU packing matrix this afternoon.

— Karthik
Capacity & Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@bluefjord.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for Zephyr model (32k)

Maya —

Thanks again, attaching the short sim summary and recommended next steps. TL;DR recommendations for procurement doc:

1) Preferred path for production (cost + latency): int8/q4 model variant with per-session KV kept on-GPU for hot sessions + automatic KV pruning for idle sessions. Estimated committed hardware: 3 x 48GB GPUs (reserved/pod packing) to meet 150 concurrent sessions with expected p50 ~130–150ms and p95 ~250–320ms.

2) Lower-cost compromise: fp16 model with KV offload + prefix caching. Requires NVMe-backed host and adds complexity but saves ~30–40% on committed GPUs. Expect higher tail latency; recommended for non-critical workloads.

3) Staging: 3-GPU test cluster, 1.5x concurrency (225 sessions) for 2 weeks. Run the provided workload, enable prefix-only caching, and collect p50/p95 and cache hit rates.

Next steps:
- We will send a short SOW and a recommended reserved GPU count (incl. pricing tiers) by Wed.
- Can we lock a 30m sync on Tue 10am PT to go over the SOW and procurement timeline?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood-kv-sim-3scenarios.pdf, bluefjord-observed-profiles.csv)
